dependency: The Mission Subject's continuing delegation to the client acting under the Mission: the Subject's account is active and the Subject has not withdrawn the delegation from that client.

source.description: The deployment's configuration-backed identity source (config/identity.json: each principal's status and the clients it has withdrawn its delegation from), read by the authorization server's identity-state resolver and re-read without a restart.

observation: One read of the identity source: the Subject's account status and the clients it has withdrawn delegation from, as of that read.

governs.scope: Existing Missions whose recorded authority source is user-delegated, and every action they authorize: each issuance under them (approval, code redemption, refresh, token exchange, child and expansion derivation) and each action decided under them.

recovery: Reliance resumes when an observation within the bound shows the Subject active and the delegation held. A suspended Mission resumes only through an authorized lifecycle operation, after which every remaining check still applies. Re-enablement is a basis for future issuance only: it restores no authority removed through Containment and revives no terminated Mission.
responsibility_transfer: None: a user-delegated Mission's authority is the Subject's own. Work that must continue without the Subject is a new Mission approved under an authority source that names its successor, through an authorized process; the original approval's attribution is unchanged.

external_change_bound.start: The identity source records the change (identity.json's changed_at for the principal).
external_change_bound.end: No action under a governed Mission can begin an effect: every issuance gate and every PDP decision under it refuses, and the reconciler has suspended or revoked the Mission.
external_change_bound.already_started: An action whose PDP permit was issued before the change completes within that request. A permit relied on beyond it expires no later than its valid_until: at most max_staleness_seconds after the observation it relied on, and at most reconciliation_max_lag_seconds after the observation the last complete reconciliation acted on. Access tokens already issued run to their expiry, but every issuance and every decision they reach refuses.
external_change_bound.path: Detection: the resolver re-reads the source at least every detection_period_seconds, and each reconciliation pass reads it afresh. Evaluation: each issuance gate and each PDP decision evaluates the latest read synchronously. State change: a reconciliation pass at least every reconciliation_period_seconds commits suspend or revoke. Downstream reliance: an observation is relied on for at most max_staleness_seconds, and the PDP refuses once the last complete reconciliation rests on an observation older than reconciliation_max_lag_seconds. Permit validity: no permit outlives the observation it relied on or the reconciliation it relied on. A composition may schedule either period faster than declared, never slower: the authorization server refuses to start otherwise. The bound holds for a successful observation path; when the source cannot be read or a reconciliation fails, the PDP refuses once the reconciliation lag passes its bound, no later than reconciliation_max_lag_seconds after the change, and the issuance gates once the observation passes max_staleness_seconds.
